subtype: Approach: following family expectation without examining it [Pitfall]
passage:
Rajni pulled a crumpled paper from her son's bag and smoothed it on the kitchen table.
“Twenty-one out of fifty?”
“Give it back.” Eshaan didn't look up. “Don't tell Papa. I'll fix it.”
“You used to draw until midnight. Now you say nothing at all. Eshaan, do you even like physics?”
“It doesn't matter. Papa and Bhaiya are engineers. That's the plan.”
“Who asked you if you wanted it?”
“Nobody had to.” He rubbed the edge of the table. “I sit in class and my head is somewhere else. I hid the last two tests as well.”
Rajni sat down slowly. “Two tests. And I only noticed today.”
He finally glanced up. “Are you angry?”
“No. I'm wondering why none of us asked.”

qa.q: What score did Eshaan get on the physics unit test?
What might Eshaan be feeling as he says nobody had to ask?
qa.a: Resigned and ashamed: he hid his marks and assumed the family's plan left no room for what he wanted.

qa.q: What could Eshaan try instead, and why?
qa.a: He could talk honestly with his mother or a school counsellor about what interests him and what other streams offer, because choosing without asking whether he likes it is why he is bored and hiding marks.

qa.q: How does the situation look to Rajni?
qa.a: Rajni sees her son hiding marks and going quiet, and realises the family assumed his path without asking him, so she may feel worried and a little guilty.

grounding: A student picks the science stream because his father and elder brother are engineers, never asks himself whether he likes it, and hides poor marks.
